text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-The cabinet meets today to solve the issue of the religious audiovisual media. Media workers and unionists urge for wide participation in afternoon protest sit-in in front of the prime minister's office.
-Leftist MP Sadeq lodges appeal with the Constitutional Council against the parliamentary elections.

-Prosecutor Mirza demands up to one year's jail for Beirut journalist for allegedly slandering workers at Rene Muawwad Foundation headed by the late president's wife by accusing them in an article of dealing with Israel.
-Speaker of Parliament Berri expresses his disagreement with the way the government is handling the audiovisual media issue.
-Minister of displaced people Jumblatt says billions of Lebanese pounds "evaporate" in the ministry of finance, Beirut airport and the official radio station.
-Palestinean protest in front of UNRWA offices to demand improvement of social services to the refugees.
-Israeli forces in south Lebanon undertake a wide search operation for a missing soldier.
-Israeli gunners shelled the hills of Jabbour and Abi Rashed in southeastern Lebanon.
-A number of parliamentary deputies demand international organisations to work for the release of four people kidnapped by Israel.
-The government deploys 3,800 policemen to protect itself against the media workers' protest sit-in.
-Maronite Patriarch Sfeir says the government must secure freedom for all citizens without any tyranny or bias.
